born.why: The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately when hunger is critical (>98), distinguishes between known good and bad fruits using diary history, uses tasting to gather information on unknown fruits while managing risk, and carries known good fruits for efficiency up to a pantry limit.

The code prioritizes safety by tracking per-species harm rates, carries known-good fruits to save time until the pantry fills, and cautiously tastes unknown fruits only when hunger justifies the risk of poisoning, while avoiding approaches to potentially toxic or already-explored neutral fruits.

The code prioritizes survival by eating immediately only when starvation is imminent (>98 hunger) or when the risk of waiting outweighs the risk of poison (>85 hunger). It distinguishes between known bad (never eat), known good (carry to pantry if space permits), and unknown (taste to learn unless starving). The `wants` function avoids known poisons and only approaches unknowns when there is a safety buffer, preventing energy waste on dangerous foraging attempts.

This code improves survival by prioritizing starvation avoidance, using trait-based inference for unknown fruits to reduce blind tasting risks, and managing pantry space to ensure continuous food availability.
